title: Identified Horizons for Treated-Cohort Effects under Underidentified Autoregressive Untreated Means in Staggered Panels

gap_reasons: The contribution remains confined to population identification under an exact common cohort-mean AR restriction; it supplies neither inference under an estimated fiber and dimension nor a practically implementable treatment of the general polynomial optimization problems.

Those omissions, together with the absence of an application demonstrating that the nonmonotone recovery and joint-set geometry materially change empirical conclusions, constrain the leading-journal score despite the field-level identification result.

proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the exact p-d+1-or-never ambiguity frontier, stable exact-order attainment, polynomial criteria for later coordinates and summaries, and a full observed-law sharpness theorem. Two review rounds repaired finite-horizon, normalization, global-fiber, and joint-nuisance issues; the final math and decision reviews were clean. The result was downgraded only because clearing the field package threshold would require a separate rank-adaptive inference, certified computation, and empirical-application program.
tldr: When a common AR\((p)\) law for untreated cohort means fits a finite staggered-adoption panel but its coefficients are not identified, which in-panel ATT cells are nevertheless identified? The proposal seeks an exact answer: for a finite cohort \(g\), the first ambiguity over \(1\le h\le T-g+1\) is the first Krylov state that fails to annihilate the global coefficient-fiber directions and occurs by horizon \(p-d+1\) or every remaining in-panel cell is identified; later cells and weighted summaries are classified by finite polynomial-coefficient tests; and every remaining ambiguity is attained by one full causal-law completion indexed jointly by \((\phi,\eta)\in F\times\Xi\) with the identical observed panel distribution. This matters because coefficient rank failure need not invalidate all later effects, while separate marginal bounds can ignore dependence induced by the shared coefficient and joint early-cohort nuisances.
gap: Existing causal forecasting, PCR, and behavioral-informativity results establish that prediction may survive model underidentification and provide sufficient span conditions, but the inspected theorem texts do not give an exact dimension-refined finite-panel causal horizon, post-failure coordinate recovery, or sharp observed-law ATT sets for a nonsingleton common-AR fiber.
fill: Prove the finite-panel \(p-d+1\)-or-never frontier and stable attainment when that horizon is observed, characterize every in-panel coordinate and linear summary through companion-polynomial coefficients, derive sharp joint images, and prove the exact full-law projection over one common coefficient and one joint early-cohort nuisance profile.
